verdict.rationale: Exa has a dedicated rate-limits docs page stating that endpoints have default rate limits, and that page lets users review usage and set lower per-key limits. Billing is self-serve pay-as-you-go: users load credits and can configure auto recharge. However, the evidence shows no actual limit numbers, no concurrency caps, and no self-serve way to raise rate limits. missing for 10: specific documented per-endpoint rate-limit values, documented concurrency caps, a self-serve path to raise limits, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can read documented rate limits and concurrency caps with a self-serve upgrade path

citations.quote: Our API endpoints have default rate limits to ensure reliable performance for all users.
Review usage and set a lower limit for an individual key.
Add credits, configure auto recharge, and view invoices.
Exa is pay-as-you-go. There is no subscription and no minimum spend: you load credits and are charged per request
